correctness.rationale: The complete set of divisors of 2^a p is partitioned into (2^i,p 2^(a-i)); deficit sigma(n)-2n equals 2^(a+1)-1-p. Both boundary indices i=0,a are excluded by size/parity, and the exact quotient condition p=(2^(a+1)-1-sum2^i)/(1+sum2^(a-i)) is necessary and sufficient. A height bound yields a<=27. A complete 17550-triple and 80730-quadruple enumeration with exact integer divisibility and trial primality gives the three composite triple quotients and the three prime quadruple quotients. A direct divisor-sum certificate proves the least witness. The included verifier fully checks the enumerated scope; nothing is inferred about a>27.

value.rationale: Omission-pair count is a natural representation complexity measure in strongly pseudoperfect and near-perfect number theory. After the known first two-pair example, this complete low-exponent three-/four-pair spectrum is a mathematically motivated finite next-order classification. A sharp first-four-pair threshold, uniqueness and the absence of three-pair occurrences even when four-pair examples appear show an unexpected nonmonotone realization pattern. The bound follows mathematically from the first witness; it is not an arbitrary random cutoff. The result provides precise new reference data without claiming paper-sized generality.
